records.usage_note: Japanese ぎゅうにゅう refers specifically to cow's milk; scope of the EN/VN pair needs review.
はな can also mean nose; 花 denotes a flower.
あめ can also mean candy; 雨 denotes rain.
はし can also denote chopsticks; 橋 denotes a bridge.
Vietnamese áo sơ mi is narrower than general English shirt; intended garment type needs review.
はは commonly refers to one's own mother when speaking to others; not a direct respectful address.
うれしい often means glad or pleased about an event; broader happy senses need review.
やさしい may mean easy or kind; 易しい denotes not difficult.
きれい can describe beauty or cleanliness; context determines the meaning.
かく can refer to writing or drawing; 書く denotes writing text.
たすける often means aid or rescue someone in difficulty; ordinary assistance may use a different expression.
ことば may mean language, words, or speech; intended scope needs review.
ちがう is verbal: AとBはちがう means A and B differ.
なぜなら introduces an explanation, often followed by a reason and から; clause placement matters.
こんにちは is commonly a daytime greeting.
おねがいします is a polite request formula, not a standalone equivalent in every use of please.
すみません may be apology, excuse me, or attention-getting; use an apology context for sorry.
アパート may denote a narrower housing type than generic apartment; intended housing scope needs review.
となりのひと means the person next door; broader neighborhood scope needs review.
そぼ commonly refers to one's own grandmother when speaking to others; not a direct respectful address.
